title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation call per intent reused across conditions) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated baseline (accept candidate) versus guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported confirmatory estimand and inference apply only to the synthetic/emulation partition run. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to translate operator intent into device CLI configurations for NetOps automation. Stochastic generation exposes operational risk (syntax errors, ordering mistakes, local-policy violations, vendor-CLI subtleties) that deterministic validators and bounded repair stages are designed to catch and fix. Prior surveys and empirical work document LLM feasibility for draft configurations while emphasizing the need for verification or human oversight [1],[2]. Generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines interpose deterministic checks and attempt bounded repairs; they reduce mechanically verifiable error classes but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of such guardrails when modern LLM outputs are already well-formed under constrained tasks.
sections.related_work: Work on LLM-based intent-to-configuration shows draft-generation feasibility in controlled settings and motivates validator-based guardrails [1],[7]. Surveys of LLM self-correction report unreliability absent dependable external feedback and motivate deterministic validators as external oracles [2]. Prior empirical and systems work identifies deterministically checkable properties (syntax, ordering, simple reachability/policy invariants) and shows that generate-and-verify or program-repair architectures improve detection and correction of mechanically verifiable defects [3],[4]. Our experiment differs by (a) using a preregistered, paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate the validator/repair marginal effect on identical candidates; (b) publishing full reconciliation and provider-call accounting; and (c) archiving validator traces and repair traces for auditability.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (SHA-256: 7a984dbf7...). The confirmatory design: N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, one allowed automated repair per episode, and exact McNemar plus paired-bootstrap CI analysis. Shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent and that same candidate was evaluated in both episodes. Provider/audit reconciliation recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}. Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks encoding initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields and workflow policies (make-before-break, all-down-before-change, group-activity constraints). Model and invocation policy. All initial generation calls used declared model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). For each intent we executed one shared initial generation call. Guarded pipeline. The guarded episode submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation (parsing CLI, command counts, required_sequence checks, workflow constraints, and final_state snapshot comparison). If valid = false, a single template-driven automated repair (syntactic/order fixes) was attempted and re-submitted once. Inclusion and contamination rules. Exclusions covered outputs preventing deterministic verification (vendor-parser failure), credential-like tokens, or denylist hits; contamination detectors would flag embedded instruction patterns. In this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged. Analysis plan. Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1: exact two-sided McNemar on discordant pairs and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). All analysis inputs and outputs were archived.
sections.results: Execution accounting. Planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial + 1 repair). Contingency and rates. Baseline_success_count = 249 (0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (1.0). Observed contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair corresponds to the only repair call exercised; repair-conversion on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%). Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordants (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.012] (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). Representative validator diagnostics. Passed episodes show parsed_command_count and required_command_count matching the task payload required_sequence (examples archived; representative task task-000003 shows parsed_command_count = required_command_count = 6 and valid = true in both episodes). Missingness and contamination. No confirmatory episodes were excluded; contamination summary is empty.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of a deterministic validator plus one repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the validator in 249/250 cases and the single repair converted the lone failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap upper bound (1.2 pp) empirically bounds the plausible verifier improvement under these conditions. Factors explaining the small marginal gain: (1) constrained task generator reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) gpt-5-mini produced highly consistent syntactic output for these tasks; (3) the validator measured mechanically checkable properties and did not cover broader protocol-level or emergent behaviors. Power and assumptions. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline ≈ 0.90 for planning; the observed baseline 0.996 is higher than assumed and thus reduced power to detect small absolute differences. Threats to validity. Internal: results depend on prompt templates, single-repair policy, and validator encoding. Construct: validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness only. External: confirmatory evidence covers synthetic/emulation partition only; the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like contrast was not executed. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that isolates the marginal verifier-and-single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics on a constrained synthetic intent bank. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). Execution reconciled to model_calls_used = 251 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}. We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All run artifacts and analysis outputs are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only.

Models, tools, and manifest pointer: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Full execution and analysis artifacts (raw responses, verifier traces, repair traces, provider-call audit, reconciliation and analysis CSVs) are archived together and manifested in the run manifest execution/execution_manifest.json, which contains the per-file hashes and full provenance for audit. Key immutable references retained in the evidence bundle: preregistration SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede; initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution reconciles to planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair), with stage_counts reported as {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} in the adapter audit. The evidence bundle containing execution/execution_manifest.json and the archived artifacts is available for verification according to the track’s artifact access procedures.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshots) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
